Product: Screened 20 mm aggregate (Demolition concrete)
Category: Demolition concrete
Subcategory: Screened Demolition concrete
Materials: concrete, natural aggregate remnants
Condition: waste
Dimensions: 20 mm graded fraction
Weight: 22.0 kg
Origin: structural demolition crushing
Reuse applications: road subbase, lean concrete feed, gabion infill
Compliance: IS 383 recycled aggregate review, IS 456 durability screening, EN 12620 aggregate grading
Description: This waste lot comes from structural demolition crushing and is primarily composed of concrete and natural aggregate remnants. In typical reuse screening it is associated with high compressive mineral matrix, non-combustible behavior, and abrasion-resistant aggregate skeleton. Typical units measure 20 mm graded fraction and weigh about 22.00 kg each, which makes the batch relevant for road subbase and lean concrete feed or gabion infill. Residual steel is removed to limit magnetic contamination. Reuse teams commonly review it against IS 383 recycled aggregate review and IS 456 durability screening before release.

product_descriptions: This waste lot comes from structural demolition crushing and is primarily composed of concrete and natural aggregate remnants. In typical reuse screening it is associated with high compressive mineral matrix, non-combustible behavior, and abrasion-resistant aggregate skeleton. Typical units measure 20 mm graded fraction and weigh about 22.00 kg each, which makes the batch relevant for road subbase and lean concrete feed or gabion infill. Residual steel is removed to limit magnetic contamination. Reuse teams commonly review it against IS 383 recycled aggregate review and IS 456 durability screening before release.

This recycled lot comes from slab cutting and breakup and is primarily composed of concrete and cement paste. In typical reuse screening it is associated with non-combustible behavior, abrasion-resistant aggregate skeleton, and alkaline pore structure. Typical units measure 0-40 mm blended grading and weigh about 28.00 kg each, which makes the batch relevant for lean concrete feed and gabion infill or temporary hardstand. Chloride and sulphate screening is important before concrete reuse. Reuse teams commonly review it against IS 456 durability screening and EN 12620 aggregate grading before release.

Particle grading controls compaction and drainage performance. Reuse teams commonly review it against EN 12620 aggregate grading and EPD-ready recycled content declaration before release.

This reclaimed lot comes from selective deconstruction of timber roofs and is primarily composed of sal timber. In typical reuse screening it is associated with good screw-holding capacity, repairable surface checking, and moderate thermal insulation. Typical units measure 3000 x 150 x 75 mm and weigh about 24.00 kg each, which makes the batch relevant for secondary structural framing and furniture stock or interior wall battens. Moisture content should be checked before joinery reuse. Reuse teams commonly review it against IS 883 timber structural review and FSC reclaimed claim before release.

This reclaimed lot comes from joinery dismantling and is primarily composed of teak timber. In typical reuse screening it is associated with repairable surface checking, moderate thermal insulation, and high machinability. Typical units measure 2400 x 200 x 30 mm and weigh about 18.00 kg each, which makes the batch relevant for furniture stock and interior wall battens or stair tread fabrication. Old nail holes and notches reduce net section capacity. Reuse teams commonly review it against FSC reclaimed claim and PEFC chain-of-custody note before release.

Typical units measure 2700 x 100 x 50 mm and weigh about 11.00 kg each, which makes the batch relevant for interior wall battens and stair tread fabrication or acoustic slat panels. Species identification improves grading confidence. Reuse teams commonly review it against PEFC chain-of-custody note and IS 401 preservative treatment check before release.
